Furthermore, the text is referenced across multiple analytical and hermeneutical treatises of the early Pali tradition, appearing in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2 Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi) as well as four chapters of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 4 Desanāhāravibhaṅga, Ne 9 Catubyūhahāravibhaṅga, Ne 10 Āvaṭṭahāravibhaṅga, and Ne 37 Sāsanapaṭṭhāna) [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus reveal 22 internal Pali correspondences across five texts, with no cross-language parallels meeting the threshold [DharmaNexus]. Prominent overlapping passages occur in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Catuttho bhāgo, matching segments §1.1–2.4) and the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo, matching segments §1.1–4.5), alongside recurring citations in the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* (§0.4–1.4), the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā* (§0.4–1.4), and the grammatical work *Saddanītippakaraṇaṃ* (*Dhātumālā*, §2.1–2.4) [DharmaNexus].
